title: Off-Cycle Performance Snapshots and Calibration Process
author: Sofia Martinez
body:
Overview

Purpose:
This page sets out how Redwood Inference runs off-cycle performance snapshots and the calibration step that follows. A snapshot is a short, evidence-based assessment used when a documented evaluation is needed outside the quarterly or annual review cycle, for example a role change, a manager transition, an accelerated promotion request, a serious performance concern, or reintegration after leave.

Scope:
- All full-time and fixed-term employees, globally.
- Contractors on engagements under 90 days are excluded unless the manager needs evidence for a conversion decision.
- Run by People Ops together with the employee's manager and the manager's manager.

Why we run off-cycle snapshots:
- Give consistent, time-boxed evidence for ad-hoc talent decisions.
- Reduce bias with a shared rubric and a normalization step.
- Keep the effort small (2-4 artifacts plus a calibrated rating).

Definitions:
- Snapshot: a 7-14 calendar day evidence collection and assessment for one person.
- Snapshot Outcome: No Action, Focus Plan (30-60d), Promotion Recommendation, Role Alignment Review, or Offboarding Recommendation.
- Calibration Review: a meeting where managers compare snapshots and normalize ratings before People Ops finalizes outcomes.

Triggers (examples):
1) Manager requests promotion acceleration.
2) Manager change or reassignment.
3) Return from leave >60 days needing role/level confirmation.
4) Clear performance regression needing a documented short-term intervention.
5) Role misalignment found during onboarding or a transfer.

Process:
1) Initiation (Day 0)
   - Owner: Manager or People Ops.
   - Fill in the Snapshot Intake Form (Appendix A): trigger type, proposed outcome, core evidence, deadline (7-14 days).
   - SLA: People Ops acknowledges within 1 business day.
2) Evidence Collection (Days 1-10)
   - Owner: Manager + Employee.
   - At least 2 of: PRs or design docs with review comments; customer/partner feedback; product metrics or experiment results; 2-3 peer notes using the standard template; on-call or post-incident notes.
   - Optional: training certificates, mentor notes, delivery metrics.
3) Manager Assessment (within 2 business days of evidence close)
   - Owner: Manager.
   - Score Skills, Impact, Autonomy and Collaboration on a 1-5 scale (1-2 Below, 3 Meets, 4 Exceeds, 5 Strongly Exceeds).
   - Deliverable: one-page summary and suggested outcome.
4) Peer/Counterbalance Review (optional; recommended for promotions)
   - Cross-functional peers add short corroborating comments via the micro-feedback form.
5) Calibration Review (within 10 business days of manager assessment)
   - Facilitated by People Ops.
   - Participants: Manager, Manager's Manager, People Ops representative; a Leveling Panel member joins for promotions.
   - Agenda: pre-reads, 10-15 minutes per snapshot, normalization, outcome recorded.
   - Decision authority: the Manager's Manager signs off; People Ops records the decision.
6) Outcome communication (within 2 business days of calibration)
   - Manager tells the employee in a one-on-one, with People Ops copied; Focus Plans and Promotion Recommendations come with a written plan or packet template.
7) Follow-up and Closure
   - Focus Plans are tracked weekly; promotion packets are assembled within 30 days and go through the standard promotion workflow.

Timelines and SLAs:
- Acknowledgement: 1 business day.
- Evidence window: 7-14 calendar days (default 10).
- Calibration completion: within 10 business days of manager assessment.
- Outcome communicated: within 2 business days of calibration.
- Total end-to-end target: 28 calendar days.

Standardized Rubric:
- Skills: 1-5
- Impact: 1-5
- Autonomy: 1-5
- Collaboration: 1-5
- Attach evidence links and a one-line summary per dimension.

Normalization guidance:
- Compare against the mean rating per level from the Leveling Panel page.
- If the suggested outcome is more than 1 level away from the distribution, the Manager's Manager presents supporting evidence at calibration.
- Promotions need at least two independent artifacts beyond the manager's own account.

Decision matrix (example):
- Average score <2.5 -> Focus Plan or Offboarding Recommendation.
- Average score 2.5-3.5 -> No Action or Development Focus Plan.
- Average score 3.6-4.2 -> consider stretch assignments or role alignment.
- Average score >4.2 -> Promotion Recommendation (with corroboration).

Table: Snapshot outcomes and owner actions

| Outcome | Required artifacts | Next owner action | Timebox |
|---------|--------------------|-------------------|---------|
| No Action | Assessment summary | Record in HRIS; normal cadence | 0-30 days |
| Focus Plan | Assessment + 2 evidence links | 30-60d plan, weekly check-ins | 30-60 days |
| Promotion Recommendation | Assessment + 3 artifacts + peer notes | Promotion packet, Leveling Panel | 30 days |
| Role Alignment Review | Role description + gap analysis | Manager & Hiring Partner propose options | 14-30 days |
| Offboarding Recommendation | Incident logs + formal warnings | Escalate to People Ops + Legal | immediate |

Manager responsibilities:
- Submit the intake form for eligible triggers.
- Gather at least two artifacts and request peer feedback where needed.
- Complete the rubric with evidence links and a short narrative.
- Present the case at calibration.
- Deliver the outcome and follow-up plan.

People Ops responsibilities:
- Check paperwork and redact privacy-sensitive items.
- Schedule calibration and send pre-reads.
- Record outcomes in HRIS and keep the audit trail.
- Publish an anonymized quarterly summary of snapshot outcomes by team.

Appeals and Escalations:
- Employees may ask for clarification within 5 business days of the outcome.
- An employee who disputes a Promotion Recommendation denial can appeal to the Leveling Panel within 15 business days.
- Managers may raise timeliness concerns with the People Ops Director.

Privacy and evidence handling:
- Snapshot documents are confidential and kept in the HRIS restricted folder with role-based access.
- Redact sensitive customer data unless sharing is explicitly permitted.

KPIs:
- Time to outcome (target 28 days).
- Share of snapshots leading to promotion recommendations.
- Variance vs. quarterly reviews (target < 10%).
- Employee pulse survey after closure.

Appendix A - Snapshot Intake Form (example):

---
trigger: "manager_promotion_request"
proposed_outcome: "promotion_recommendation"
requested_deadline: "2025-10-20"
artifacts:
  - "PR: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/1187"
  - "Customer email: redacted@example.com"
peer_reviewers:
  - "eng-peer@example.com"
notes: "Employee led the batching scheduler rework."
---

Appendix B - Manager communication templates:
- Promotion approval: "After calibration we are recommending your promotion to [level]. People Ops will assemble the packet and confirm compensation."
- Focus Plan start: "We are starting a 45-day development plan focused on [skill], with weekly check-ins."
- No Action: "We are not changing your level or compensation at this time and will keep reviewing progress in regular check-ins."

Governance:
- People Ops reviews this process annually.
- Quarterly anonymized summaries go to People Ops leadership and Engineering HR partners.
